continuity.arc_goal: Complete linked workflow SDK foundation and design Promise Objects API with compile-time type safety for handling long-lived external computations

progress_update.summary: We squashed the entire linked-workflows branch from 31 commits to 1, updated to latest shared-core proto, then designed the Promise Objects Rust SDK API. The design session produced a comprehensive API spec covering StartRequest (unified linking type replacing RunRequest), #[start] attribute for marking linkable handlers, T-suffix context gating for linking capability, PromiseContextT with compile-time resolve() enforcement, and WorkflowContextT as a new context type.
progress_update.goal: Complete linked workflow SDK foundation and design Promise Objects API with compile-time type safety
accomplished: Updated to latest sdk-shared-core proto (LinkCompletionNotification rename, field reordering)
Designed Promise Objects API: StartRequest replaces RunRequest, #[start] attribute for linkable handlers
Designed PromiseContextT<S> with SealedCanResolve for compile-time resolve() gating
Designed WorkflowContextT<S> — new context type enabling linking from workflows
Established that linking requires T-suffix contexts (ObjectContextT, PromiseContextT, WorkflowContextT)
progress_update.now: Design doc finalized and saved. API design discussion complete — all major decisions made.
next_steps: Implement #[start] macro attribute with validation rules
Implement PromiseContextT<S> with SealedCanResolve and ctx.resolve()
Add sys_resolve to sdk-shared-core VM trait
Switch shared-core from path dep back to published version before PR
constraints: No mock VM in codebase — integration tests require real Restate container
Discovery type remains VirtualObject — server doesn't distinguish promise objects
decisions: Squashed all 31 commits into single commit rather than splitting typed completion handlers out
Backup branch linked-workflows-backup preserved for safety
start_linked() returns impl Future (not DurableFuture) — link establishment is fast
result() returns impl DurableFuture — child completion can be long, needs select! support
Cancellation wraps Invocation via From — compile-time API narrowing for VO contexts
link() generic over T: From<Invocation> — type inference at call site
Invocation does NOT implement InvocationHandle — resolved vs unresolved separation
on_completion only via ObjectContextT path — no runtime panic risk
Handler input type: Result<T, TerminalError> where T: serde::Deserialize
T-suffix naming: ObjectContextT, RunRequestT, WorkflowClientT, RunT, CompletionHandlerFnT
sys_link returns LinkHandle with link_completion_handle
API: run_linked(req) on workflow client returns Request with linked:bool=true, .send() emits both OneWayCallCommand + CreateLinkCommand
API: unlink() on workflow client, fire-and-forget, emits RemoveLinkCommand
API: .send() returns impl InvocationHandle regardless of linked flag — CreateLink completion handled internally
StartRequest replaces RunRequest — unified type with start_linked() and on_completion()
#[start] is purely client-side code gen signal — no discovery metadata changes, valid on any non-shared Object or Workflow handler, rejected on #[shared] and Service
Linking gated to T-suffix contexts only — ObjectContextT, PromiseContextT, WorkflowContextT
PromiseContextT adds resolve() via SealedCanResolve sealed trait — compile-time enforcement
No enforced entry point name — user marks handlers with #[start], multiple allowed on objects
Workflow run is implicitly #[start], explicit #[start] on workflow allowed but redundant on run

Should #[start] be required on at least one handler for PromiseContextT objects?
Should InvocationHandle::invocation_id() be removed since resolve() exists?
Should docs/ working files (session logs, reviews, specs) be excluded from the PR commit?
risks: Server-side promise objects (ResolveCommand) not yet implemented
Three repos need coordinated branches for PR
